Explicit counterexample entirely within hypotheses: \(n=2,m=p=1,Q=[-1,1]\), \(K_0=B_2(0,1/4)\), \(K_u(t)=A_tK_0\) for the volume-one shear \(A_t(x,y)=(x,y+tx)\), \(-1\le t\le1\). The original \(K=A_1K_0\) has vertical chord centers \(x\), so this is precisely its Steiner linear parameter system. The \(p=1\) mixed-area definition gives \(\Pi^\circ_{Q,1}(K_0)=B_2(0,1)\); determinant-one covariance gives \(\Pi^\circ_{Q,1}(K_u(t))=A_t B_2(0,1)\). Take rotationally invariant measure \(d
u=\mathbf1_{B_2(0,1)}dx\), a \(\gamma=\infty\)-concave density on its convex support. Polar integration with \(v=	an\vartheta\) gives \(A_
u(t)=|B_2\cap A_tB_2|=\int_{-\infty}^{t/2}[1+(v-t)^2]^{-1}dv+\int_{t/2}^\infty(1+v^2)^{-1}dv=\pi-2\arctan(t/2)\) for \(t\ge0\). Thus the asserted \(s_\infty=1/(nm)=1/2\) concavity of \(f=\sqrt{A_
u}\) fails: \(f\prime\prime(t)=[tA_
u(t)-1]/[4A_
u(t)^{3/2}(1+t^2/4)^2]>0\) at \(t=1/2\), since \(\pi>3\) and \(2\arctan(1/4)<1/2\) imply \(A_
u(1/2)>5/2\). The package wrongly elevates the lead source's convexity at fixed transverse coordinates to joint convexity over all spatial coordinates. The known Steiner endpoint monotonicity is consistent with the counterexample and is not refuted.
